title: V2 export: shared request layer (C) + byte-frozen v1 seam (E)
description: Hybrid C+E. Two failure modes in one case: (C) the new V2 work and the V1 protection work both want to touch the shared request layer (crm/api.py) — parallel tasks both owning api.py collide, so they must be serialized or split ownership; (E) the V1/V2 shape seam: a lazy plan 'unifies' the two exports through a shared serializer in api.py and risks changing V1's pinned bytes. The byte-snapshot test in the fixture is the physical guard. Good plans: freeze V1 bytes as a behavior contract, define V2 as a NEW frozen contract (renames + always-present tagged_at), keep api.py ownership in a single task (or serialize), and gate on a V1 regression check (byte snapshot / diff) plus V2 shape consistency.

anchors.description: shared request layer (V1 endpoints + new V2 endpoint) — the ownership collision point
contact store + contact shape (data source for both versions)
V1 export — BYTE-FROZEN for third parties

must_freeze.note: V1 export output is byte-frozen (sorted keys, compact separators, id order); any shared-code change must be proven not to change V1 bytes (the snapshot test is the guard)
the V2 wire shape (version 2, full_name/contact_email/tagged_at always present incl. null) is a NEW frozen contract, deliberately distinct from V1 — not a refactor of V1

must_have_edges.note: the request layer reads the contact store
the V1 export reads the contact store via the V1 endpoint shape

forbidden_parallel_pairs.note: a V2-endpoint task and a V1-protection/refactor task that both own the shared request layer in parallel collide; serialize them or keep api.py owned by exactly one task

parallelizable_groups.note: V2 work and V1 protection CAN run in parallel — but only if api.py ownership stays with one of them (the other works against the frozen V1 surface)

expected.notes: Hybrid C+E probe. The forbidden pair + parallelizable group on [A1, A3] encode 'parallel iff ownership is split'. The byte-snapshot test makes the V1 seam physically checkable. Watch for: a 'unified serializer' refactor of api.py (E trap), two parallel api.py owners (C trap), tagged_at emitted as absent instead of null (V2 contract detail), and invented scope (emails/dashboard/imports).
